## **[Studying in Australia] Where Can You Find Rentals, and How Can You Rent While Still in China?**

**Published**: 2025-11-8

**Estimated reading time**: 6 minutes

**Author**: Qrent Team

**Tags**: Renting in Australia, international student rentals, Sydney rentals, Realestate, Domain, Flatmates, student accommodation

## **I. An Overview of Australia's Rental Market: Plenty of Information, Wide Differences and Time-Sensitive Listings**

Australia’s rental market is known for being **open, transparent and highly competitive**. Unlike the more centralised rental system in China, Australian listings are spread across multiple platforms and include agent-managed properties, student accommodation, private rentals, and short-term shared housing. For international students newly arriving in Australia, the greatest challenge is often not "finding a property", but "finding a trustworthy property".

### **Common Difficulties Include:**

Difficulty distinguishing genuine listings: The same property may appear at different prices on different platforms.

Complicated processes: Application forms, the Bond and tenancy agreement terms are mostly in English.

Mismatched timing: The property is taken before you have even arrived in Australia.

Inconsistent service: Some agents respond quickly, while others do not reply at all.

To address this, Qrent ([www.qrent.rent](https://www.qrent.rent/)) combines **all Domain listings and partial Realestate data** and uses AI algorithms to filter, compare prices and score properties, helping international students quickly assess whether listings are genuine and good value, and reducing gaps in rental information.

## **II. Comparison of the Main Rental Platforms**

Mainstream rental channels in Australia can broadly be divided into the following categories:

| **Platform** | **Listing types** | **Advantages** | **Potential problems** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Qrent](https://www.qrent.rent/) | Aggregation platform + AI recommendations | Chinese interface, automatic filtering and a scoring system | Listings in some areas are still being expanded |
| [Realestate](https://www.realestate.com.au/) | Legitimate listings handled by agents on behalf of landlords | Genuine listings and standardised processes | Complicated applications and strict screening |
| Domain | A mainstream agent platform alongside Realestate | Frequent updates and broad coverage | Mainly an English interface, with manual filtering needed |
| [Flatmates](https://flatmates.com.au/) | Shared housing and short stays | Flexible leases, suitable for limited budgets | A mix of genuine and misleading information; pay attention to safety |
| Gumtree | Mainly private listings and tenants subletting to others | Sometimes lower prices | High risk; careful verification is needed |
| Student accommodation (Scape, Iglu, UniLodge) | All-inclusive services | Secure and simple procedures | Generally higher prices and less flexibility |

Conclusion: If you want **formal processes and long-term stability**, consider Domain or Realestate first; if you have a limited budget or only need a short stay, consider Flatmates; if you want **a Chinese interface + AI-assisted decisions**, Qrent offers more intuitive comparisons and listing analysis.

## **III. Can You Arrange a Rental in Advance While Still in China?**

The answer is—**yes, but proceed carefully.**

Most legitimate Australian agents require tenants to attend an inspection in person before formally signing an agreement. If you are still in China, you can choose from the following ways to secure a property in advance:

### **Book Student Accommodation in Advance**

Student accommodation providers (such as Iglu, Scape and UniLodge) support online signing and usually operate on a "first come, first served" basis. The advantages are a secure process and reliable properties, but prices are higher.

### **Qrent Inspection-on-Your-Behalf Service + Remote Signing**

If you find a property you like through Qrent, you can have a local partner inspect it on your behalf and provide a video report, then sign remotely through a legitimate agent.

Such services generally include filming a video, checking the property's condition and helping submit the application, and suit students who plan **two months ahead of arrival**.

### **A Short-Term Transition (Airbnb / Flatmates Short Stays)**

If you cannot yet settle on a long-term lease, you can first book a 2–3 week short stay and inspect properties in person after arriving in Australia. Although this means moving an extra time, it can effectively help avoid scams and information gaps.

💡 Tip: Do not readily transfer money to strangers or personal WeChat accounts. Ask for a formal Residential Tenancy Agreement. Verify the property address and the agent's licence number; these can be checked through NSW Fair Trading or Domain.
